title: Personal Checking: Combining the Limits on a Single-Dispute Provisional Credit
content:
## Rule of combination

Where a Personal Checking account has exactly one electronic-transaction dispute in submitted status, the provisional credit posted on it equals the smallest of the limits that apply to it. Each applicable limit is taken at its own full value; limits are compared with one another, never subtracted from one another or added together, and a limit that does not apply to the disputed debit is simply left out of the comparison. Where the account does not have exactly one submitted dispute, this single-dispute sizing yields no credit.

The figures involved all carry two decimal places, so the smallest one is posted exactly as it stands, without rounding. The credit is posted only once it is owed under the ordinary dispute timing.

## Illustrations (hypothetical limits)

| Limits that apply | Credit posted |
|---|---|
| 80.00 and 60.00 | 60.00 |
| 80.00, 60.00 and 25.00 | 25.00 |
| 40.00, 60.00 and 0.00 | 0.00 |
| 60.00 and 60.00 | 60.00 |

## Points of judgement

- The lowest figure governs even when it is zero; a zero figure means nothing is credited provisionally.
- Adding a further applicable limit can only keep the credit where it is or lower it, never raise it.
